data.claim: With the snapshot on, a cold load is slower than parsing the log, on the real log and at 200k to 1M synthetic events, so default-off is right. A parsed event costs 1.4 to 2.5 KB of retained memory, not the 736 bytes the knob doc says, so a 200,000-event ceiling holds about 300 to 500 MB rather than 147 MB.
data.falsifier: Median cold read_all with the snapshot on is below off on the real log, measured in fresh processes with the snapshot verified in use (0 lines parsed, every shard seeded).
data.mechanism: The snapshot does not avoid the expensive work: `_seed_from_snapshot` re-hashes every shard's real bytes (the hash is the trust check) and then unmarshals all objects, which costs more than C json parsing of the same lines, and the frames sit in memory beside the decoded objects, hence the higher peak. The 736-byte figure came from B86's bench, whose events are tiny `task.added` rows; real events carry gate evidence (880 bytes on disk per event here).

data.body:
From the PS-snapshot-calibrate critic round 4 (deepseek, LOW). (1) ddflow/infra/log/_parse.py _SNAP_SWEPT grows by one Path per events dir in a long-lived process: cap it. (2) _collect_stale_snapshots counts the current snapshot in the total but never evicts it, so an existing snapshot over a lowered snapshot_max_mb survives until the log changes: delete it when it alone exceeds the cap. Add a test for each.

Superseding note: the two findings above were fixed in PS-snapshot-calibrate. The 5th critic round raised two new LOW ones, deferred here: (a) _collect_stale_snapshots: total -= mine_size is skipped when mine.unlink() raises (use missing_ok / decrement outside the suppress); (b) the _SNAP_SWEPT bound is not atomic across threads (overshoot by the number of concurrent readers).

Added by PS-snapshot-calibrate round 6 (LOW, deferred): (c) a regression test that exercises the non-atomic _SNAP_SWEPT bound; (d) knob_changed.log.snapshot.toml says old snapshot files stay readable when the snapshot is on, but log.snapshot_max_mb can collect other versions' files: reword the note, and add ddflow/templates/upgrade/** to this item's globs if it is still unreleased.

chunk_findings.detail: With `[log].snapshot = true` and enough events that `bytes_out + _SNAPSHOT_SLOT > cap` during the write loop, the new `raise ValueError("the snapshot is over [log].snapshot_max_mb")` escapes `_write_snapshot`. Nothing in this diff adds a `ValueError` handler, so the caller's read now aborts because the optional snapshot exceeded the file cap, rather than merely skipping the cache write. A log large enough to exceed the configured cap (for example lowering `log.snapshot_max_mb` below the default while leaving events high) will make the whole read fail.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_read.py:_write_snapshot

chunk_findings.detail: The new function gates deletion on `self.log_cfg.snapshot`, but the effective switch is `self._snapshot_enabled()` and the file imports `SNAPSHOT_ENV` for the per-process override. In a process with `[log].snapshot = false` but `SNAPSHOT_ENV` enabling snapshots, the first `_read` of a log dir passes the config check, adds the dir to `_SNAP_SWEPT`, and deletes all `read-snapshot*.bin` files; `_snapshot_enabled()` is still true afterward, so the persisted snapshot that the override promised is gone. The opt-in snapshot benefit is destroyed on the first read of every new process.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_read.py:_discard_disabled_snapshots

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier over-cap branch is unchanged: `mine.unlink()`, `_SNAP_COVERED.pop(...)`, and `total -= mine_size` are all inside one `with contextlib.suppress(OSError)`. If `mine.unlink()` raises `OSError` (for example a sibling process already removed `mine`, so this process gets `FileNotFoundError`), the subsequent lines are skipped while `total` still includes the current file's size. The later loop then sees `total > max_bytes` and unlinks every file in `others`, even though after excluding the missing current file the remaining files are under the cap, over-deleting valid snapshots.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_read.py:_collect_stale_snapshots

chunk_findings.detail: The bound check is still not atomic: `len(_SNAP_SWEPT) >= _SNAP_SWEPT_MAX`, the later `_SNAP_SWEPT.clear()`, and `_SNAP_SWEPT.add(self.dir)` are separate operations. Multiple threads with distinct `self.dir` can all read a length just below the maximum, skip the `clear()`, and then each add its own directory, overshooting the claimed bound by up to the number of concurrent readers. The intended bounded cache is therefore not actually bounded under concurrency.

chunk_findings.detail: The migration note says the per-shard append facts in `.ddflow/local/shardmeta` "stay on unless log.reuse_parsed = false", but the change itself makes `_guard._shard_meta` follow `reuse_parsed` and `cache_writes` only. For a configuration with `log.cache_writes = false` and `log.reuse_parsed = true`, the note tells the operator shardmeta remains on, while the new guard condition (both knobs) disables it. The note therefore omits `log.cache_writes = false` as another input that stops shardmeta, making the upgrade guidance incorrect/incomplete for that setting.

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test still does not exercise the non-atomic bound it is meant to guard. This test prepopulates 300 entries and calls `EventLog.read_all()` once from a single thread, so it never interleaves those operations and would still pass even with that race.
